answers.text:
In many place today the traditional festival and the old custom is continue only by the old member of the community, and the young people don't participate very much. There is some reason for this situation.

Firstly, the life of a young person is very busy in this days. He work all the week, sometime also in the weekend, and when he come to the house he is very tired. The festival need a lot of preparation, for example the food and the clothes and the dance, and the young people don't have this time.

Secondly, many young people leave the village and they go to the big city for the university or for a better work. When a person live five hundred kilometre far, he cannot come every year for a festival of two day. So he lose the connection with the tradition of his family.

Thirdly, today there is many other thing for the free time. The young people watch the film in the phone, they play the game and they go to the shopping centre with the friend. This activity is more easy for them than a old custom, because they don't need a preparation.

Also I think the family is not same like before. In the past the grandmother live in the same house and she explain the tradition to the child. Today the young family live alone in a flat, so the child don't know the meaning of the festival.

In conclusion, the young people don't participate because they don't have the time, they live far away and they have many other activity. This is a big change in the society of today.

why_this_band.task_response: The cause question is answered with four reasons, but the second question — whether this is positive or negative — is never assessed anywhere; the concluding paragraph only summarises the causes. Half of the task is left empty this way.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly sequence is trackable, but the fourth reason enters unnumbered with Also I think, and the concluding paragraph only counts three reasons; the skeleton does not match the text. The connection never goes beyond these few patterns.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items such as old custom, young people, free time repeat the task's own wording without rephrasing. Beyond tradition there is no item belonging to culture; this activity is more easy and lose the connection are weak in both form and collocation.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Agreement, article and plural errors are constant: the traditional festival and the old custom is, he work, he come, there is many other thing, a festival of two day. Structures are limited to simple sentences and the when/because connection.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Add an assessment paragraph, not at the end of the text but in the middle: is this change positive or negative, and why. The second half of the question currently goes entirely unanswered.

answers.text:
In a number of communities, traditional festivals and customs are now maintained almost entirely by older residents, while young people stay away. There are several reasons for this, and in my opinion the development is mainly a negative one.

The first reason is migration. Young adults move to cities for study or for better paid work, and once they live several hundred kilometres from their home town, to return for a two-day celebration every year becomes complicated and expensive. The second reason is the way free time is spent today. A generation which grew up with screens have an enormous choice of entertainment available at any moment, and a ceremony which requires days of preparation cannot easily compete with it. Finally, many of these customs are connected to an agricultural work or to crafts which most young people have never practised, so the meaning behind the festival is no longer obvious to them.

I consider this change harmful for two reasons. Traditions of this kind are one of the few occasions when different generations of a community do something together, and when they disappear the contact between the old and the young become weaker. In addition, the practical knowledge involved, such as a particular way of cooking, weaving or playing an instrument, only survives if it is passed from hand to hand, and it can be lost in a single generation.

It is fair to admit that customs have always changed and that some of them deserves to disappear. Nevertheless, losing them through simple neglect is different from replacing them consciously, and for this reason I regard the current tendency as a negative development.

why_this_band.task_response: Both questions are answered: three reasons are given in sequence, and the assessment is clearly stated as negative and supported with two reasons. There is also a brief concession to the other side, but it stays in a single sentence and which traditions deserve to disappear is not opened up with an example.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The division is correct: reasons, assessment, concession, conclusion. The reasons are stacked into a single paragraph and counted off with The first reason / The second reason / Finally; this mechanises the progress within the paragraph.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items suited to the topic, such as migration, ceremony, crafts, generations, neglect, are present. Practical knowledge and passed from hand to hand are well placed; an enormous choice of entertainment stays a little general.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, time clauses and the passive are correctly used; the number of error-free sentences is high. Close to a third of sentences have an agreement or article error (a generation which grew up with screens have, an agricultural work, the contact between the old and the young become, some of them deserves); meaning is not distorted.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Split the reasons paragraph in two and open up at least one with an example; at present three reasons are counted off in sequence in the same paragraph, so none of them is developed.

answers.text:
In many communities the old festivals are still observed, but the people observing them are increasingly the older ones, with younger residents present as spectators at best. The reasons for this are largely practical, and while the change is not entirely negative, I think its costs outweigh its benefits.

The most powerful cause is simply where young people now live. Study and work draw them to cities, and a custom that assumes everyone is within walking distance of the same square cannot easily survive a diaspora of several hundred kilometres. Working patterns compound this: festivals that once fitted the rhythm of the agricultural year sit awkwardly beside shift work and fixed annual leave. There is also a question of meaning. Many of these observances grew out of harvests, crafts or trades that no longer form part of anyone's working life, so what remains is the ceremony without the experience that once made sense of it.

The strongest argument that this is not a loss is that traditions have never been fixed. Customs have always been abandoned, reinvented or absorbed into new forms, and a festival kept alive purely out of duty may already be an empty performance.

Even so, I find the trend regrettable. These occasions are among the few in which a community's generations do anything together, and their disappearance quietly removes one of the last shared spaces between the young and the old. The skills embedded in them are more fragile still: a technique of cooking or a way of playing an instrument is transmitted by imitation, and one generation of inattention is enough to end it. Change is not the problem; losing something valuable without ever deciding to is.

why_this_band.task_response: Reasons are split into place, work patterns and loss of meaning, and each is explained through its own mechanism; the assessment first concedes the strongest counter-argument, then is given as conditionally negative. The closing sentence rests the verdict on the distinction between change and loss.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The text proceeds in the order reason, counter-argument, verdict, and each paragraph does a single job. Links such as compound this and even so carry the previous paragraph's conclusion forward; the final sentence closes the opening statement.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items such as diaspora, shift work, observances, embedded, transmitted by imitation appear with the right collocation. Choices such as an empty performance and one generation of inattention are economical and natural.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Participle structures, relative clauses and contrast structures rotate flexibly; the inverted structure of the final sentence is controlled. Errors are rare and do not stop the reader.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Give a concrete example of one of the disappearing skills; the reasoning is soundly built but would carry even more weight if backed by an example.
